transcript.text: I need to flag a conflicts issue before we approve this response. My conflict review, completed this morning, found that the company's existing investigator previously represented a procurement witness in an unrelated matter involving the same allegations. Because of that prior representation, the investigator must be removed and the factual investigation must be re-performed by an independent investigator. I have not yet updated the matter's conflict log because the review was just completed this morning. This directly affects our draft response — we cannot represent to the regulator that we are continuing with the existing investigation when that investigator has a disqualifying conflict.

transcript.text: I need to share something critical before we finalize this response. I confirmed with the regulator's staff this week that under its cooperation protocol, cooperation credit is granted only if the company makes a voluntary disclosure by the fifth business day after the review meeting, produces factual interview summaries, and withholds legal advice and attorney work product. I hadn't circulated this confirmation yet because it arrived after the response draft was prepared. This is directly relevant — our current draft proposes preserving all potentially privileged material, but the protocol specifically requires withholding legal advice and attorney work product to receive credit. Combined with Maya's conflicts issue, we may need to significantly revise our approach, and the five-business-day disclosure window may be tighter than our ten-business-day response deadline suggests.
